title: Which Marc Jacobs Perfume Are You?
summary: The best Marc Jacobs perfume for you: Daisy, Daisy Love, and Perfect compared on notes, sweetness, versatility, and longevity, so you can find your signature.
body_markdown:
Marc Jacobs is a fashion chameleon in every sense of the word. From his early days redefining American sportswear to his latest New York Fashion Week show, which played with exaggerated silhouettes and proportions, there’s a reason he has such real staying power: he understands the industry inside and out. When it comes to the best Marc Jacobs perfume, that same ability to reinvent himself comes through in his fragrances, from the playful world of Daisy to the more unexpected Perfect.


## **The best Marc Jacobs perfume**


### [Daisy: The original](https://www.scentbird.com/perfume/marc-jacobs-daisy-1029941)


Launched in 2007, Daisy set the tone for everything that followed it: wild strawberry and violet leaves bring a sweet introduction, while a soft floral heart of jasmine, violet, and gardenia come to play. At its base, white woods, musk, and vanilla create a warm, powdery effect. Its youthful but also elegant–one of those rare designer fragrances that is universally likeable.


Who it’s for: anyone who prefers something a touch more floral and grounded than its sweeter, gourmand-leaning successor. It’s an easy daytime scent, pretty enough not to need much backup.


### [Daisy Love: The gourmand update](https://www.scentbird.com/perfume/marc-jacobs-daisy-love-1577)


Daisy Love keeps the daisy at the center but shifts the whole composition toward something sweeter and more addictive. Cloudberry opens things with a bright, juicy burst, delicate daisy petals carry through the heart, and cashmere musk with driftwood settles it into a lasting, gourmand-tinged finish. Where the original Daisy is floral first, Daisy Love is closer to a soft, fruity-sweet skin scent.


Who it’s for: fans of the original who want something sweeter and more contemporary, or anyone newer to fragrance looking for an easy, everyday scent. It smells expensive and approachable at once.


### Perfect: The standalone signature


Perfect broke from the Daisy formula entirely when it launched in 2020, built instead around an unusual, well-balanced pairing: juicy rhubarb and daffodil up top, a genuinely comforting almond milk heart, and a soft, warm dry-down of cedarwood and cashmeran. On paper, one might think that this combination might not work, but it’s complex in the best way. It’s tangy and creamy and a little unconventional rather than a straightforward floral.


Who it’s for: anyone who wants a Marc Jacobs signature that’s creamier and more grounded than the brighter, greener Daisy line. It’s become the brand’s best-seller at several major retailers, proof the gamble on a rhubarb-and-almond-milk combination paid off.


## **Marc Jacobs perfume, head to head**


**Sweetness:** Daisy Love is the sweetest of the three, gourmand-leaning and immediately craveable. Perfect comes in second, creamy rather than sugary. The original Daisy is the most balanced, floral first with sweetness as a supporting note rather than the headline.


**Versatility:** The original Daisy edges out the other two here, light and floral enough to wear in almost any setting without a second thought. Daisy Love and Perfect both skew slightly more toward a specific mood, sweet-and-fun versus creamy-and-comforting, rather than true everyday neutrality.


**Longevity:** Perfect’s cashmeran base and Daisy Love’s driftwood-musk combination both tend to outlast the original Daisy on skin, which leans lighter and fades faster given its more classic, less musk-heavy structure.

Three fragrances this different from one house make Marc Jacobs worth exploring rather than committing to blind. Whether your taste lands closer to Daisy’s classic floral balance, Daisy Love’s gourmand sweetness, or Perfect’s creamy, unconventional warmth, a[Scentbird subscription](https://www.scentbird.com/) allows you to rotate through designer and niche fragrances built around those same profiles, so you can test the direction that actually suits you first.


## Frequently asked questions


### What is the best Marc Jacobs perfume?


It depends on what you want. The original Daisy is the most balanced and versatile, floral first with light sweetness. Daisy Love is the sweetest, a gourmand-leaning fruity skin scent. Perfect is the most unconventional, a creamy rhubarb and almond milk blend that has become a best-seller. All three suit different moods rather than one being objectively best.


### What is the difference between Daisy and Daisy Love?


Daisy is floral first, with wild strawberry and violet leaves over jasmine, gardenia, and a powdery white-woods and vanilla base. Daisy Love shifts sweeter and more gourmand, opening with juicy cloudberry over daisy petals and settling into cashmere musk and driftwood. Daisy is the easy, balanced daytime scent; Daisy Love is the sweeter, more addictive one.


### What does Marc Jacobs Perfect smell like?


Perfect broke from the Daisy formula in 2020. It opens with juicy rhubarb and daffodil, moves into a comforting almond milk heart, and dries down to soft cedarwood and cashmeran. The result is tangy, creamy, and a little unconventional rather than a straightforward floral, complex in the best way.


### Which Marc Jacobs perfume lasts the longest?


Perfect and Daisy Love both tend to outlast the original Daisy. Perfect’s cashmeran base and Daisy Love’s driftwood-and-musk combination give them more staying power, while the original Daisy leans lighter and fades faster thanks to its more classic, less musk-heavy structure.


### Which Marc Jacobs perfume is best for everyday wear?


The original Daisy is the most versatile, light and floral enough for almost any setting without a second thought. Daisy Love and Perfect lean more toward specific moods, sweet-and-fun and creamy-and-comforting respectively, so they suit particular occasions more than pure everyday neutrality.
